newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil Range reports on indepent review.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range reports on indepent review.

text.p: The independent committee reviewing Anvil Range Mining Corp's Faro lead and zinc mine recommends that higher metal prices are needed before the mine can reopen, Anvil Range said on Thursday.
Anvil Range said its board of directors has confirmed its decision to suspend mining operations starting December 20.
The committee report said low metals prices were partly responsible for the shutdown, Anvil Range reported.
The report said ore reserves as projected appear to be a reasonable forecast for the life of the mine.
The report also found that strip mining at the site fell behind because trucks were not available, which reduced the amount of ore released to the mill.
The report said "the actual mine operations generally give a good impression, with haulage roads, working places and grade control effort all of a good standard."
At the Grum deposit, the grade is projected to be about seven precent combined lead and zinc, the report said.
This grade was anticipated in the original mine plan and is less than the grade found over the past year.
But the metallurgical performance of the Grum deposit has been less than forecast.
The report concluded that recovery rates of 77 percent for lead and 73.5 percent for zinc should be expected over the life of the operation.
The report also said Faro operations were over budget for 1996, with the largest proportion attributed to the mill department.
As mill performance is stabilized in 1997, related costs should be reduced and longterm strip mining costs will decline over the life of the mine, Anvil Range said.

Based on revised mine plans and recently achieved concentrate grades and metal recoveries, the best course of action to restart the mine is to wait for metal prices to rise above US$0.31 per pound of lead and US$0.47 per pound of zinc, the report said.
Anvil Range has said it will continue to run its mill on stockpiled ore to produce about 50 percent of the intended output of 480,000 tonnes per year of zinc and lead concentrate.
